body.text: Middesk is a San Francisco B2B software company selling business-identity infrastructure — verifying businesses for financial-services onboarding, and filing state and federal registrations on their behalf. Its customers are banks, lenders and payments companies onboarding business accounts of their own. The product line is software and filing services: it does not lend, and it does not hold customer funds.

Identity is settled on every axis the registries can speak to. The submitted name and address both match state registrations, entity type is confirmed against a filing, and there is an active registration in the state of the submitted address — not merely somewhere. A Delaware corporation formed in March 2018 operating from California, registered in five states, is an ordinary and coherent shape.

Registration status reads mixed — active in California and Idaho, inactive in Illinois, unresolved in Delaware and New Jersey. That is housekeeping for a company registered across many states rather than a sign of lapse: a business withdraws from a state it has stopped operating in, and the inactive one is not the state of operation.

gaps.point: Whether the company is in good standing in Delaware
gaps.wouldAnswer: Delaware publishes no good-standing sub-status for any company, so no order will return one. A Certificate of Good Standing from the customer is the only route.

gaps.point: The status of the Delaware and New Jersey registrations
gaps.wouldAnswer: Both searches ran and reached no conclusion — our limit, not a fact about the company. A re-run of the registration search may clear them.

body.text: A submitted person matches an officer named on a state registration — the strongest control-person evidence registry data produces, because it ties a named individual to a filing the state holds rather than to anything the customer supplied. California names three officers, and two of them are the people the customer submitted.

gaps.point: Whether the person named on the website is the person submitted
gaps.wouldAnswer: The check ran and reached no conclusion — the site does not name them in a form it could read, which is different from naming someone else.
gaps.noAction: the officer match on the California registration covers this ground more authoritatively.

gaps.wouldAnswer: No beneficial-ownership insight exists in the catalog. Ownership is only ever implied from the people filings happen to name, and an officer is not an owner. If your policy requires a UBO determination, this record cannot satisfy it by any order.

body.text: It is visibly operating rather than merely registered. The submitted address is commercial and deliverable, the website is reachable, and the domain registrant corroborates the business at high confidence. The site independently matches the submitted name, address and email address — three separate agreements, not one restated three ways.

The address footprint is ten addresses across the frequency bands: three shared with twenty businesses or fewer, two in the middle, five shared with more than a hundred. Read cold the five look like a shell pattern; read against a company registered in five states they are its registered agents, and the quiet addresses alongside them are what distinguishes the two — a shell has the crowded addresses without the others.

Both the website and the third-party profiles were supplied by the customer rather than discovered. The profiles are reachable, which is worth little on its own; what carries weight is that the domain registration corroborates the business without the customer's help.

Screening is clean where it matters most. Watchlist returned no hits against all fourteen sanctions and denied-party lists — OFAC, BIS, DDTC and ISN — and PEP returned none. No prohibited industry was identified, no risky keywords were found, and there are no bankruptcy filings.

Adverse media is where care is needed. The provider returned no adverse media and scored the business low risk, but fourteen articles were pulled in against three individual names and then dismissed — the Kyle Mack matches include a Louisiana murder case, and the Kurt Ruppel match is a personal website. These are name collisions, not findings, and they are worth knowing about only so that nobody rediscovers them later and reads them as hits.
Open liens were found and litigation records were returned. This is the only thing on the record pointing at the business rather than at the limits of the data.

gaps.point: What the liens and litigation actually are
gaps.wouldAnswer: The record establishes that they exist and stops there — no amounts, no dates, no indication of whether they are satisfied. Nothing in the catalog goes further; it takes a lien and litigation detail order.
